testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: If you must drive in reverse, what should you do?

options.text: Drive as fast as possible to finish quickly.
Exit the truck and walk the path to check for obstacles.
Use only the passenger side mirror.
Stick your head out the window and look backward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit the truck and walk the path to check for obstacles.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, walk around your vehicle to check for hazards. Use both side mirrors while backing. Always back up slowly.

questions.question: You are driving slowly in a construction zone and see a worker near the road. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Always drive slowly in construction zones. Slow down even more if workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: Your wheels are spinning when you accelerate on a slippery surface. What should you do?
questions.explanation: If your wheels spin while accelerating on a slippery surface, remove your foot from the accelerator.

questions.question: How should you change lanes?
questions.explanation: Change lanes slowly and smoothly. This gives other drivers time to react. Always signal when changing lanes.

questions.question: Which of these is acceptable during a pre-trip tire inspection?
questions.explanation: Check that tires have enough tread. Front tires need at least 4/32 inch of tread. Other tires need at least 2/32 inch. Tire sizes must match.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle unattended, what should you do?

options.text: Only set the parking brake if parked on a hill.
Let the air out of the tires by 10 percent.

questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when leaving your vehicle unattended.

questions.question: Which of these is required emergency equipment?
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles must have required emergency equipment. This includes spare electrical fuses, reflective triangles or flares, and a fire extinguisher.

questions.question: What type of brake system do most heavy-duty vehicles use?
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems. These have two separate braking systems controlled by one set of controls. Each system operates the brakes on different axles.

questions.question: On a vehicle with power steering, what should you check on the hoses?

options.text: Make sure they are connected to the battery.

questions.explanation: Inspect power steering hoses, pumps, and fluid levels. Look for leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT help prevent aggressive driving?

options.text: Not expecting any delays on your drive.
Keeping a safe distance from other vehicles.
Keeping your hands on the steering wheel.
Avoiding hand gestures at other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not expecting any delays on your drive.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, expect delays and allow extra time. Drive at a safe speed, keep a safe following distance, avoid gesturing at other drivers, and keep both hands on the wheel.

questions.question: When braking at 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag can add how much to your total stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your total stopping distance.

questions.question: If other vehicles are having trouble passing your truck on a road with two or more lanes, you should:
questions.explanation: Stay in the right lane if your truck is going slower due to a heavy load. Let other vehicles pass you using the left lane.

questions.question: Skids happen when:

options.text: Tires lose their grip on the road.
There is too much weight in the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tires lose their grip on the road.
questions.explanation: Skids happen when tires lose grip on the road. This can be caused by over-braking, over-accelerating, over-steering, or driving too fast.

questions.question: A pre-trip inspection:

options.text: Should be done the same way every time.
Should be done differently every time.
Does not need to include all items every time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be done the same way every time.
questions.explanation: Do your pre-trip inspection the same way every time. This helps you learn all the steps and makes sure you don't forget to check anything.

questions.question: Before going down a hill, you should shift into a ____ gear.
questions.explanation: Before going down a hill, shift into a low gear. Gravity will speed up your vehicle as you go downhill.

questions.question: If turning to avoid a hazard:

options.text: You should not brake because it could lock the wheels.
You should turn the wheel very sharply.
You should keep the brakes pressed until you pass the hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should not brake because it could lock the wheels.
questions.explanation: Do not brake while turning to avoid a hazard. Braking while turning can lock the wheels and cause a skid.

questions.question: If you think a road is becoming icy, you can check by:

options.text: Opening the window and checking the side mirror for ice.

questions.correctAnswerText: Opening the window and checking the side mirror for ice.
questions.explanation: If you think the road may be getting icy, open your window and feel the front of your side mirror, mirror support, or antenna. If ice is there, the road is likely getting icy too.

questions.question: At dawn or dusk when other vehicles have trouble seeing you, you should:
questions.explanation: At dawn or dusk, and in snow or rain, turn on your headlights so other drivers can see your vehicle.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure gets too low in an air brake system?

options.text: The brakes will be very sensitive.

questions.explanation: Pressing and releasing the brake pedal unnecessarily lets air out faster than the compressor can replace it. If air pressure gets too low, the brakes will stop working.

questions.question: When you see a construction worker near the road, you should:

options.text: Wait until construction is complete before driving.

questions.explanation: In work zones, drive at the posted speed limits. Slow down even more when workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: If you see taillights ahead while driving in fog, what should you know?

options.text: The lights may not show where the road is. The vehicle may have left the road.
You can be sure the vehicle ahead is on the road.
It may be an optical illusion.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lights may not show where the road is. The vehicle may have left the road.
questions.explanation: In fog, lights are not a reliable sign of where the road is. A vehicle's lights may be coming from a vehicle that has left the road.

questions.question: Air entering air storage tanks may contain:
questions.explanation: Air entering storage tanks usually contains water and compressor oil. These materials can damage the braking system, so tanks have drains to remove them.

questions.question: Why do some air brake systems add alcohol to the system?

options.text: To stop the brakes from squeaking.
To prevent ice from forming in the brake system.
To prevent people from breathing air from the system.

questions.correctAnswerText: To prevent ice from forming in the brake system.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator. It adds alcohol to the system to stop ice from forming in cold weather.

questions.question: When making a left turn, when should you start the turn?

options.text: Before reaching the center of the intersection.
At or after the center of the intersection.
After your rear wheels have passed the center of the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or after the center of the intersection.
questions.explanation: Wait until you reach the center of the intersection before turning left. If you turn too early, your vehicle's left side may hit another driver.

questions.question: After cargo is secured, how often should you check it?

options.text: You do not need to check it for the entire trip.
You can drive at least eight hours without checking it.
Check it every three hours or every 150 miles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check it every three hours or every 150 miles.
questions.explanation: Check cargo before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles.

questions.question: What is one way to handle blind spots?

options.text: Drive faster than other vehicles so they cannot pass you.
Stay in the left lane so you only worry about vehicles on your right.
Check your mirrors often and know where other vehicles are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors often and know where other vehicles are.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to watch traffic around you. This helps you notice if other vehicles move into your blind spots.

questions.question: Is a ramp's posted speed limit suitable for all vehicles?

options.text: Yes, it is suitable for all vehicles.
It works for some vehicles, but may be too fast for a large truck.
It is only a suggestion and can be exceeded.

questions.correctAnswerText: It works for some vehicles, but may be too fast for a large truck.
questions.explanation: Ramp speed limits are set for cars. These speeds may be too fast for large or heavy trucks. Truck drivers often need to slow down below the posted limit.

questions.question: What helps you decide when to upshift?
questions.explanation: Two things tell you when to shift up. Engine speed (rpm) tells you when to shift based on your vehicle's manual. Road speed (mph) tells you which speeds work for each gear. Check your speedometer and shift up as needed.

questions.question: What does the service brake system do?

options.text: Applies and releases the brakes when you press the brake pedal while driving normally.
Applies and releases the parking brakes.
Applies and releases the emergency brake.
Applies and releases the axle brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Applies and releases the brakes when you press the brake pedal while driving normally.
questions.explanation: Air brakes have three systems: service, parking, and emergency brakes. The service brake system applies and releases the brakes when you use the brake pedal during normal driving.

questions.question: If the brakes pull to one side when used, what does this mean?

options.text: They will be the most effective.

questions.explanation: If the brakes pull to one side, there is a brake problem that needs to be fixed.

questions.question: A distracted driver may be:

options.text: Not talking to anyone in the vehicle.

questions.explanation: A distracted driver may drift between lanes, change speeds, focus on a cell phone or map, or talk to passengers. You can spot these signs in other drivers.

questions.question: If air pressure drops to ____, a low pressure warning should have already turned on.
questions.explanation: The low pressure warning light, buzzer, or wig wag should activate before air pressure drops to 55-75 psi.

questions.question: To put out an electrical fire, you should:
questions.explanation: B:C fire extinguishers are made for electrical fires and burning liquids. Never use water on an electrical fire.

questions.question: Exhaust system parts should:
questions.explanation: Exhaust parts must not leak or be broken. A broken exhaust system can let poisonous fumes into the cab or sleeper.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver crashes ahead of you, you should:

options.text: Stop a safe distance away and tell police about the aggressive driving you saw.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop a safe distance away and tell police about the aggressive driving you saw.
questions.explanation: If you see an aggressive driver crash, stop at a safe distance, wait for police, and report what you saw.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve releases air from the air brake system, it means:
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air when pressure gets too high. If this happens, something is wrong and a mechanic should fix it.

questions.question: If your hydraulic brakes will not build pressure, you should:

options.text: Push the brake pedal down hard.

questions.explanation: If your brakes lose pressure, try downshifting, pumping the brakes, and using the emergency brake to slow your vehicle.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, belts should be:
questions.explanation: Check all belts for tightness and wear during your pre-trip inspection. Learn how much give is normal for each belt.

questions.question: When using a turn signal, you should not:

options.text: Leave the signal on long after the turn is done.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the signal on long after the turn is done.
questions.explanation: Signal early and continuously during turns or lane changes. Always cancel the signal when you finish turning to avoid confusing other drivers.

questions.question: You should not use the parking brake:

options.text: When parked on a slight slope.
When the vehicle's brakes are very hot.
When other braking systems are working well.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the vehicle's brakes are very hot.
questions.explanation: Do not use the parking brake if the brakes are hot from going downhill or if they are wet in freezing weather. Using the parking brake on hot brakes can damage them. Wet brakes in freezing weather can ice up and stop the vehicle from moving.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT required emergency equipment?
questions.explanation: All commercial trucks must have emergency equipment. This includes red reflective triangles, flares, and a fire extinguisher. A flashlight is optional equipment.

questions.question: When traction is poor, a driver should accelerate slowly:

options.text: Because it is best to always accelerate very slowly.
So they do not lose control of their vehicle.
So the driver does not accelerate faster than the vehicle ahead.
To be the last vehicle through an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: So they do not lose control of their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Speeding up too quickly on slippery roads can cause you to lose control. On poor traction roads, accelerate slowly and smoothly.

questions.question: When approaching your vehicle for a pre-trip inspection, what should you look for as a sign of trouble?

options.text: A puddle of oil under the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: A puddle of oil under the vehicle
questions.explanation: Look under your vehicle for fresh leaks of oil, coolant, grease, or fuel. Any puddle means there is a safety problem.

questions.question: When traveling down a long downgrade, you should brake by:

options.text: Mostly using the brakes and downshifting occasionally.

questions.explanation: On a downgrade, use the engine's braking effect to control your speed. Use the brakes only when needed for additional slowing.

questions.question: A convex mirror is sometimes called a ____ mirror.
questions.explanation: Large trucks often have curved convex mirrors called "bug-eye" mirrors. They show a wider view than flat mirrors, but objects look smaller and farther away than they really are.

questions.question: Cargo inside a trailer:

options.text: Does not need to be secured.
Should be stacked no taller than three feet high.
Should be secured to prevent movement in transit.
Should be loaded with the heaviest items on top of lighter items.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be secured to prevent movement in transit.
questions.explanation: Cargo must be secured so it does not move while driving. Loose cargo is dangerous to you and other drivers.

questions.question: When driving down a steep grade:

options.text: You should ride your brakes all the way down.
Shift into a higher gear as a way to slow down your vehicle.
Shift into lower gears as a way to slow down your vehicle.
The truck should be put in neutral as a way to slow down your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift into lower gears as a way to slow down your vehicle.
questions.explanation: On a steep grade, use lower gears to slow down with the engine. Use brakes only when needed to avoid overheating them.

questions.question: Black ice is:

options.text: Usually thick – about half an inch or more of ice.

questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it, so it looks wet instead of icy.

questions.question: In bad weather, many drivers:

options.text: Like to drive in front of trucks.
Like to be on the side of trucks.
Like to drive without using their lights.

questions.explanation: In bad weather with poor visibility, many drivers follow trucks closely. Increase the distance between your vehicle and the one in front if being followed too closely.

questions.question: If a vehicle is carrying hazardous cargo, placards must be placed:

options.text: Only on the front of the vehicle.
On the front, rear, and sides of the vehicle.
Only on the driver's side of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the front, rear, and sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Placards must be on the front, back, and both sides of vehicles carrying hazardous cargo. They must be visible from any direction.
